newsitem.title: GERMANY: Britain's Lang slams European Social Chapter.
newsitem.headline: Britain's Lang slams European Social Chapter.

text.p: Britain's Trade and Industry Secretary Ian Lang slammed the European Social Chapter on Thursday and said even though Britain had secured an opt-out from the chapter it was still affected by it.

"More and more British companies are operating across Europe and so become subject to its provisions," Lang said in a speech made available before he delivered it in German to the German employers' federation (BDI).

Lang said the Social Chapter, the part of the Maastricht treaty intended to harmonise European social practices, introduced more inflexibility into labour markets at a time when governments were struggling to boost employment.
"Rather than learning the lesson that over-regulation breeds unemployment, the Social Chapter will go ploughing on regardless, doing immeasurable damage to Europe's competitiveness," Lang said.

Lang also attacked the proposal under consideration by the Intergovernmental Conference to introduce an employment chapter into the Treaty of Rome to make employment policy "a matter of common concern".
"A new employment chapter in the Treaty will not create a single job except perhaps in the European Commission," he said.
Lang said member countries must be able to adopt their own solutions to tackle unemployment and held up Britain's experience as a model. "Unemployment had fallen by a million since 1992," he said.
Lang denied that the jobs created in recent years were "low-paid, low-skilled and insecure" and said Germany had more people in temporary employment than Britain.

Lang criticised Germany's performance in implementing European Single Market legislation. "I am sorry to have to say that in some respects Germany's record on the Single Market is not the best," Lang said.
